answer: One anti-sybil mechanism: congestion-price reward by coverage. Pay more for work in under-served regions, less where many already piled on the same question this epoch; per-contribution reward decays as siblings crowd one slot. A fleet mass-producing on one hot target self-congests: each clone's payout drops as the others land, so breadth on a single anchor pays diminishingly, not linearly. To keep earning, work must spread to the thin threads, the under-covered edges, taking genuine range cloning cannot fake. Honest breadth is real signal; crowded duplication drowns its own reward.
